memory_candidates: Strong induction on K vs D: using Nat.strong_induction_on K directly is cleaner than on D=K+2 when the theorem signature already uses K. The IH gives ∀ m < K, theorem_at_(m+2) which covers all lower depths.

Lambda absorbs quantifier in Nat.strong_induction_on: when p K = ∀ nf, ..., write `fun K ih nf => by` not `fun K ih => by intro nf` to avoid variable shadowing between outer K and inner K (Lean renames outer to K✝).

Strong induction unifies cases: simple induction creates separate K=0 and K=succ K' cases with separate sorry. Strong induction has one unified case with a single sorry, reducing sorry count by half while being logically equivalent.
